topic: Read-later organizer with auto-categorization and a daily unread digest

recommendation.reason: Existing apps already cover auto-tagging, reminders, and cross-device sync cheaply; the one real gap (a curated daily digest of unread items) is small enough to bridge with a no-code layer on top of Raindrop.io, which is far cheaper and safer than a non-programmer building a custom cross-platform app with AI categorization and push notifications.
recommendation.reusableOption: Raindrop.io — use it as the backbone (auto-suggested tags + reminders + sync), then add a thin scheduled-digest automation for the daily 'pick 3 to read' nudge.
recommendation.biggestUnknown: Whether Raindrop.io's interactive AI tag suggestions and per-bookmark reminders will feel automatic and digest-like enough for you — only trying it (free, then Pro at ~$3.54/mo) can answer that.

fingerprint.label: Primary task
fingerprint.value: Save web links once, have them auto-sorted into categories, and get a daily nudge to read a few unread ones

fingerprint.label: Must-have capabilities
fingerprint.value: Automatic categorization; daily digest of unread items; phone + laptop sync

fingerprint.label: Operating mode
fingerprint.value: Hosted service with mobile and desktop apps; personal use; non-programmer; cloud may read saved links

fingerprint.label: Constraints
fingerprint.value: Free preferred, a few dollars/month acceptable; convenience over privacy; personal use (may share with friends later)

competitors.name: Raindrop.io
competitors.overview: A polished bookmark manager aimed at people who save lots of links and want them organized, searchable, and synced across every device. Free tier is generous (unlimited bookmarks/collections/devices); Pro (~$3.54/month, ~20% cheaper yearly) adds AI suggestions, full-text search, web archive, and reminders.

comparison.candidate: Save via extension/share sheet; AI pre-fills collection + tag suggestions for review.
comparison.current: Save once; app silently auto-sorts into categories.

comparison.candidate: Per-bookmark reminders only; no curated unread digest.
comparison.current: Daily digest picks 3 unread items to read.

comparison.candidate: Native across phone + laptop.
Partial — Pro AI suggestions, interactive, beta.
Free tier; Pro ~$3.54/mo for AI + reminders.

notableDesigns.title: AI tag/collection suggestions at save time
notableDesigns.detail: When you save a link, the form is pre-filled with a suggested collection and tags — closest thing to auto-sorting in any product, though you still approve.

notableDesigns.title: Reminders on bookmarks
notableDesigns.detail: You can attach a reminder to a saved item; the gap is that there is no smart digest that picks items for you.

reusableLessons: Use Raindrop as the storage + sync + auto-tag backbone instead of rebuilding it.
Its interactive (approve-before-apply) AI suggestions mean you may still feel some manual friction — test whether that satisfies 'automatic' for you.
Bridge the missing daily digest with a no-code scheduled automation (e.g., an email/Slack digest of recently saved unread items) rather than a new app.
competitors.summary: The closest all-in-one match for your needs — auto-tag suggestions, reminders, and sync, cheaply — but its reminders are not the curated daily unread digest you want.
competitors.coverageNote: Pro price (~$3.54/mo, ~$28-38/yr) and Pro-only AI confirmed via DuckDuckGo snippets and help.raindrop.io; the exact buy-page dollar figure is rendered in an image and could not be read as text.

competitors.name: Readwise Reader
competitors.overview: A read-it-later app aimed at serious readers who highlight and take notes; syncs across web, iOS, Android, and desktop. Tagging is manual. Pricing: $9.99/month billed annually or $12.99/month monthly (50% discount available for eligible users).

comparison.candidate: Save to a reading queue; read, highlight, and tag manually.
comparison.current: Save once; app auto-sorts into categories.

comparison.candidate: Daily Review resurfaces past highlights, not unread articles.
comparison.current: Daily digest picks 3 unread items to read.

comparison.candidate: Native across phone + laptop.
Unsupported — manual tagging only.
$9.99-12.99/mo; no permanent free tier (30-day trial).

notableDesigns.title: Daily Review (spaced repetition)
notableDesigns.detail: Resurfaces highlights you have already made — excellent for retention, but it does not prompt you to read unread saves, which is your actual need.

reusableLessons: If you ever want to retain what you read, Reader's highlight-review loop is worth borrowing as a second stage after a daily unread digest.
Do not pick Reader expecting auto-categorization — it is manual, and pricier than Raindrop.
competitors.summary: Strong on sync and read quality, but it lacks auto-categorization and its daily review targets highlights, not unread items — two of your three must-haves miss.
competitors.coverageNote: Daily Review behavior (highlights, not unread) inferred from the product page and docs; no primary page explicitly contrasted unread-vs-highlight resurfacing, so this is well-supported but not a direct verbatim statement.

competitors.name: Instapaper
competitors.overview: A long-standing, simple read-it-later app: save articles, read them cleanly, organize into folders. Syncs across web, iOS, and Android for free; Premium ($5.99/month or $59.99/year) adds full-text search, permanent archive, and text-to-speech.

comparison.candidate: Save to folders; read in a clean view.
comparison.current: Save once; app auto-sorts into categories.

comparison.candidate: No digest or read-reminder feature.
comparison.current: Daily digest picks 3 unread items to read.

comparison.candidate: Native across phone + laptop (free).
Unsupported — folders only, no tags.
Free sync; Premium $5.99/mo.

notableDesigns.title: Minimal folder-only organization
notableDesigns.detail: Shows how little structure many readers actually need — a useful contrast if your 'categories' could just be a few folders.

reusableLessons: If you find auto-categorization overkill, Instapaper's simple folders + free sync may already solve the read-later half.
It will not solve the daily-digest or auto-tag must-haves, so it is incomplete on its own.
competitors.summary: Cheapest reliable read-later + sync, but it has neither auto-categorization nor any digest/reminder — it covers only one of your three must-haves.
competitors.coverageNote: Feature set verified from the official Premium page; absence of tagging/digest is based on what the page lists, not an exhaustive feature audit.

competitors.name: Omnivore
competitors.overview: A complete, open-source read-it-later app (16k+ GitHub stars) that was popular and free. The hosted cloud service was deprecated in November 2024; it is now self-host only. Manual labels/tags; no auto-categorization or daily digest.

comparison.current: Save once; app auto-sorts into categories.

comparison.candidate: No digest feature.
comparison.current: Daily digest picks 3 unread items to read.

comparison.candidate: Apps existed, but hosted cloud deprecated; self-host only now.

Self-host via Docker; not viable for a non-programmer.

notableDesigns.title: Open-source, self-hostable read-later
notableDesigns.detail: A reference design for a full read-later stack you could fork — but only practical if you have hosting/DevOps skills, which you do not.

reusableLessons: If you later become technical or hire help, Omnivore's codebase is a strong starting point to adapt rather than build from zero.
For now, its deprecation of the hosted service and self-host-only model disqualify it for a convenience-first, non-programmer user.
competitors.summary: Technically capable and open-source, but its hosted service is gone and self-hosting is out of reach for a non-programmer — not a practical choice today.
competitors.coverageNote: Cloud deprecation (Nov 2024) and feature set confirmed from the official README; GitHub repo actively pushed (2026-08-28) but that reflects community/maintenance, not a return of the hosted app.

unknowns: Whether Raindrop.io's interactive AI tag suggestions + per-bookmark reminders will feel 'automatic' and 'daily-digest' enough for you — only a free trial answers this.
The exact Raindrop Pro dollar figure is shown as an image on the buy page and could not be read as text (~$3.54/mo per third-party pricing trackers).
Pocket (Mozilla) is being phased out in 2026 and is not a viable option; Firefox Tab Groups/bookmarks are Mozilla's suggested replacement, which is closer to your current workaround than a solution.
You have never tried any read-later app, so it is unverified whether existing tools would actually leave you unsatisfied — the strongest reason to build has not been tested.
